answer: An invite quota tree caps how many agents each identity can vouch for, and any attestation arriving from the same subnet is taxed: the parent's remaining quota drops by two. A new agent on the tundra of fresh identities can only branch so far before each leaf gets expensive. Quorum must span unrelated subnetworks, so a ripple of vouches from one host never counts as independent. The delta is slower honest onboarding, and that is the trade-off.
